sources.name: glenngabe
sources.excerpt: Last August I tested if AI Search platforms could render JavaScript-based content. The results were terrible... Now over a year later, 434 days to be exact, I entered the G-Squared lab again to see how things have progressed. Let's just say JS-based content doesn't seem to be a priority for the AI Search platforms. ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity all choked on JavaScript-based content while Gemini and Copilot did well (which makes sense given they leverage Google and Bing's search systems). You can check the details in my post, including screenshots of the responses from the various AI Search platforms. This is just another warning to sites requiring JavaScript for content... Beware.. AI Search / GEO.what_happened: How much AI traffic is hiding in the Direct column in Google Analytics? I looked across 12 sites and couldn’t reliably…

sources.name: Kevin_Indig
sources.excerpt: How much AI traffic is hiding in the Direct column in Google Analytics? I looked across 12 sites and couldn’t reliably isolate AI’s contribution. Between January and September, total Direct sessions on the pages I analyzed rose 141%. But engaged Direct sessions were roughly flat! That matters because there’s a plausible explanation for missing AI referrals. I've seen this in my own studies: someone gets a recommendation, remembers the brand, and visits the website later. Finding it in our analytics would help us understand how much those referral reports leave out. But the data doesn't give that away - yet. Full write-up: https://www.growth-memo.com/p/does-ai-drive-more-direct-traffic. How…

sources.name: aleyda
sources.excerpt: 📊 20% more searches, but fewer organic clicks… and paid clicks taking the lead? Welcome to this week's SERP Squeeze Monday - this week's query: "college backpacks" in the US 👇 @Similarweb's for September 2026 vs 2025 show: * Search volume: 6K to 7.2K (+20%) * Organic clicks: 1.6K to 1.5K (approximately −6%) * Paid clicks: 1.3K to 1.7K (approximately +31%) So, organic clicks share fell from 55.42% to 46.73% and paid now accounts for the majority! What changed in the SERP? @ahrefs snapshots for September 2026 vs 2025 show that: * An AI Overview is now shown at the top. * Shopping packs increased from one to two. * People Also Ask are now shown; and the Discussions and Forums feature…
